headline: AI investment stays strong as higher yields test the global economy
dek: The United States is confronting surging borrowing costs, China is reopening after a disappointing holiday, while Japan and South Korea are benefiting from strong semiconductor demand.
story_title: A split global picture: expensive money, resilient chips
story_html:
United States 🇺🇸 — The immediate focus in the United States is no longer simply whether stocks can rise, but whether they can withstand a sharp increase in the cost of capital. The 10-year Treasury yield briefly reached 5.36%, close to its highest level since 2002, before easing after a well-received government bond auction. Higher yields make borrowing more expensive for households and companies, and they also reduce the relative appeal of equities. The pressure comes as investors weigh heavy public debt, volatile oil prices and uncertainty about future interest rates. ([apnews.com](https://apnews.com/article/44b75c188756038371cf3112ede9cee8))

China 🇨🇳 — China’s mainland markets are reopening today after the October 1–7 National Day holiday. Investors are returning to a less encouraging domestic-demand picture: early indicators pointed to restrained travel, softer spending per person and weak entertainment revenues during Golden Week. The Hang Seng Index fell during the closure, while analysts said the CSI 300 could face renewed selling. Beijing has introduced targeted measures, including mortgage support and selected lending programmes, but markets are still waiting for stronger evidence that consumers and property markets are recovering. The late-October Communist Party plenum may become the next major policy catalyst. ([livemint.com](https://www.livemint.com/market/chinas-weak-holiday-spending-casts-shadow-as-markets-reopen-11791417938323.html))

Japan 🇯🇵 — Japan offers a more constructive, but highly uneven, signal. The Reuters Tankan index for large manufacturers rose to plus-22 in October, its strongest reading since late 2021. Precision-machinery firms, many of which supply semiconductor producers, reported especially strong orders. However, non-manufacturers became markedly less confident as food, construction and retail businesses struggled with higher input costs, interest rates and weak household spending. In other words, Japan’s industrial economy is receiving a lift from the AI-related investment cycle, while consumer-facing businesses remain under pressure. ([marketscreener.com](https://www.marketscreener.com/news/japan-manufacturers-mood-hits-near-5-year-high-service-sector-sentiment-slumps-ce785dd9df8ff127))

South Korea 🇰🇷 — South Korea is seeing the same technology cycle more directly through trade. Recent export data showed semiconductor shipments rising sharply, supported by demand for high-bandwidth memory and other advanced server chips. Ship exports also surged, helping the country record stronger-than-expected overall export growth. This makes Korea an important bellwether for global trade: when demand for data centres rises, Korean memory-chip producers and Japanese equipment suppliers benefit. Yet the picture is not risk-free. Korea remains highly exposed to US tariff policy, Chinese demand and fluctuations in the global investment cycle. ([tradingview.com](https://www.tradingview.com/news/reuters.com%2C2025%3Anewsml_L1N3WD003%3A0-south-korea-october-exports-post-surprise-gain-on-strong-demand-for-chips-and-ships/))

Common theme: The four economies are not moving in lockstep. The United States is showing how higher yields can tighten financial conditions, China is struggling with domestic demand, and Japan and South Korea are benefiting from semiconductor investment. The connection is the global AI supply chain: it is supporting factories and exports even as expensive money and cautious consumers create headwinds elsewhere. The key question is whether chip demand remains strong enough to offset a broader slowdown.
b2_summary: The four economies show different economic conditions. In the United States, Treasury yields rose sharply, making borrowing more expensive and putting pressure on stocks. China’s markets reopened after a holiday during which consumer spending appeared weak, increasing calls for more policy support. Japan’s manufacturers became more optimistic because of strong semiconductor demand, although service businesses faced rising costs and weak household spending. South Korea’s exports benefited from strong demand for advanced memory chips and ships. The shared theme is the AI-related investment cycle: it is helping Japan and Korea, but higher interest rates and cautious consumers could still slow the wider global economy.

vocabulary.meaning: The cost of obtaining money for investment or borrowing (자본 조달 비용).
The interest rate investors receive for holding a 10-year US government bond (미국 10년 국채 수익률).
How easy or difficult it is for people and companies to borrow and spend (금융 여건).
Spending by consumers and businesses inside a country (내수).
An event or decision that may trigger a major market reaction (정책 촉매).
The prices businesses pay for materials, energy and other operating needs (투입 비용·원가).
A country, company or indicator that signals wider economic trends (경기 선행 지표 또는 풍향계).
Advanced memory chips designed to move large amounts of data quickly, especially for AI systems (고대역폭 메모리, HBM).
A period when businesses increase or reduce spending on equipment and capacity (투자 사이클).

concept.title: Term premium
concept.explanation: The extra interest investors demand for holding a long-term bond instead of a short-term one. It can rise when investors worry about inflation, government debt or uncertainty, pushing long-term borrowing costs higher even without a central-bank rate hike (기간 프리미엄).

quiz.question: Which economy is currently showing the clearest benefit from strong demand for advanced memory chips in its export data?
quiz.explanation: South Korea’s export growth has been strongly supported by demand for advanced server memory chips, including HBM.

one_sentence: The world economy is being pulled in two directions: AI-driven semiconductor investment is accelerating, while expensive money and cautious consumers are holding growth back.
